chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Umayyah (Isa), from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever preserves his omission and completes it, then there is no Sajdat al-Sahw (two prostrations of forgetfulness) upon him. For the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) prayed Dhuhr with the people for two Rak'at, then he was forgetful and gave Salam. So Dhul-Shimalayn said to him, 'O Messenger of Allah, has anything been revealed regarding the Salat?' He said, 'And what is that?' He said, 'You only prayed two Rak'at.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'Are you saying the like of his words?' They said, 'Yes'. So he (peace be upon him and his family) stood up and completed the Salat with them and prostrated with them the two prostrations of forgetfulness.'

He (the narrator) said, 'I said, 'What is your view of the one who prays two Rak'at and thinks that they are four, so he gives Salam and departs, then remembers after he has gone that he only prayed two Rak'at?'' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should restart the Salat from its beginning.'

He (the narrator) said, 'I said, 'So what was the matter that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did not restart the Salat, but rather he completed with them what remained of his Salat?'' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did not leave his seat. So if he had not left his seat, then let him complete what was deficient from his Salat, when he had preserved the first two Rak'at.'

key_terms.ذُو الشِّمَالَيْنِ: A companion of the Prophet, known as 'Possessor of the Two Lefts'

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for Sajdat al-Sahw if one realizes a mistake after leaving the prayer spot?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi distinguishes between minor forgetfulness (sahw) where the worshipper remains in the prayer spot, requiring only two compensatory prostrations, and major error where departure necessitates restarting the prayer entirely. Shia jurists emphasize this distinction to highlight the Prophet’s practical application of ease in worship, contrasting it with stricter views that might require full repetition. The narration underscores the importance of maintaining continuity in ritual acts when possible, reflecting the Shia principle of facilitating religious obligations.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at Bin Mihran who said,

‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘The one who safeguards his omission and he completes, so upon him are the two Sujūd for the omission (Sajda Al-Sah’w), for Rasool-Allahsaww prayed Al-Zohr Salāt with the people as two Rak’at, then omitted, so hesaww offered Salām. So Zul-Shimalayn said to himsaww, ‘O Rasool-Allahsaww! Has anything (new) been Revealed with regards to the Salāt?’ So hesaww said: ‘And what is that?’ He said, ‘But rather yousaww prayed two Rak’at’. So Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘Are you all saying the like of his words?’ They said, ‘Yes’. So hesaww completed the Salāt with them and perform Sajdah with them the two Sajdahs of omission’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘I said, ‘What is yourasws view of the one who prays two Rak’at and thinks that these two were four, so he greets and leaves. Then he remembers after having gone then he (remembers), rather, had prayed two Rak’at?’ Heasws said: ‘He should re-commence the Salāt from its beginning’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘I said, ‘So what was the matter Rasool-Allahsaww did not re-commence the Salāt, and rather hesaww completed it with them what had remained from hissaww Salāt?’ So heasws said: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww had not departed from hissaww seat. So if he had not departed from his seating, then let him complete what was deficient from his Salāt, when it was so that he had safeguarded the first to Rak’at’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Sama‘ah ibn Mehran who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘If one knows the kind of mistake he has made, he completes it, and Sajdah (prostration) for mistake is not necessary for him. The Messenger of Allah performed al-Dhuhr Salah (prayer) with people as two Rak‘at, then he mistakenly said Salam (the phrase of offering greeting of peace). Dhu al-Shamalayn asked him, “O Messenger of Allah, is anything revealed about Salah (prayer)?” The Messenger of Allah asked, “Why is that?” He said that it is because you performed two Rak‘at. The Messenger of Allah then asked others, “Do you also say what he says?” They replied, “Yes, he is right.” The Messenger of Allah stood up, completed Salah (prayer) with them and performed two Sajdah (prostration) with them because of mistake?

He (the narrator) has said that I then asked, ‘What do you say about the case of one who performs two Rak‘at and thinks that it is four, then says Salam (the phrase of offering greeting of peace) and moves away; then remembers after moving away that he has performed two Rak‘at? He (the Imam) said, ‘He performs it again from the beginning?

He (the narrator) has said that he then asked, ‘Why did the Messenger of Allah not perform again? He only completed with them whatever remained of his Salah (prayer). He (the Imam) said, ‘It is because the Messenger of Allah had not left his place. If one does not leave his place, he completes what is deficient of his Salah (prayer), provided, he has secured the first two Rak‘at?”
